full_judgment:
(i) It is not a judgment of reversal 

 (ii) The impugned judgment and decree is a proper judgment of reversal. 

 24. The facts of that case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the instant case, in view of the fact that the CS recorded tenants heirs, the defendants Nos. 7 and 10 by adducing evidence supported the defendant's case of surrender and had admitted the possession of the defendant all through in the suit land. In view of the above the decision referred to by Mr Khan is not applicable in the instant case. Mr Khan further cited the cases of Ranjit Kumar vs Shamsuddin Biswas, reported in 1997 BLD 58, 1997 BLD (AD) 47,1997 BLD (AD) 195 and submitted that the appellate Court judgment was not a proper judgment of reversal. He submitted that the judgment is not sustainable in law. On perusal of the trial Court judgment and as well as the judgment impugned in the Rule it appears that the appellate Court upon discussions and consideration of the evidence on record reversed the finding of the trial Court and allowed the appeal. I find that the impugned judgment is a judgment of reversal. I have reason to believe that the plaintiff totally failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land and the suit was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The plaintiff having had failed to mention the date of dispossession the suit was barred by limitation.
